interest: Japan's 2600th anniversary, Axis rhetoric and Hawaii surveillance.
overview: Decimal file 894.415 (covering April 1940 and November 1 to December 16, 1940) documents the international, diplomatic, and domestic security ramifications of the celebrations commemorating the 2600th anniversary of the founding of the Japanese Empire. Spanning State Department telegrams, consular despatches, press translations, and U.S. Army intelligence assessments, the records trace how the imperial milestone was orchestrated and perceived across Tokyo, Berlin, occupied China, and the Territory of Hawaii. Key subjects include Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's delicate navigation of diplomatic protocol and presidential greetings in Tokyo amidst rising Japanese chauvinism; Adolf Hitler's public embrace of Japan's 'new order' in East Asia following the Tripartite Pact; the staging of imperial loyalty rituals in occupied Tsingtao; and U.S. military surveillance of overseas Japanese delegations and Hawaiian Nisei, accompanied by sharp skepticism toward local dual-citizenship expatriation campaigns.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew submits a detailed report on the 2600th imperial anniversary celebrations in Tokyo, enclosing official speeches and imperial rescripts.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits an extensive account of the two-day national celebration of the 2600th anniversary held in the Imperial Palace plaza in Tokyo on November 10 and 11, 1940. He describes the grand ceremonial pavilion, nationwide synchronized banzai cheers, ancient Nara-period court dances, cold banquet traditions, and city-wide street festivities. Grew notes that the French Ambassador observed Emperor Hirohito nodding in apparent approval during Grew's diplomatic corps address advocating peace and the well-being of mankind. He also points out the curious omission from local English newspapers of the Emperor's second rescript calling for international peace.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5172 from Grew on the Celebration of the 2600th Anniversary

subfiles.about: Headquarters Hawaiian Department intelligence report analyzing overseas Japanese participation in the Tokyo celebrations and the Hawaiian Nisei dual-citizenship expatriation campaign.
subfiles.summary: This confidential U.S. Army intelligence document ('Comments on Current Events - No. 4') provides an in-depth analysis of the participation of over 5,000 overseas Japanese, particularly from Hawaii and the mainland, in the 2600th anniversary conventions in Tokyo. The report highlights Japanese Foreign Ministry efforts to instill racial superiority and nationalistic loyalty, citing Lieutenant General Hamada's lectures to visiting Nisei and the creation of the Overseas Japanese Central Society. It then presents a scathing critique of the Hawaiian Japanese Civic Association's 50,000-signature expatriation petition presented by Delegate Samuel W. King, arguing that it was a disingenuous public relations campaign aimed at appeasing white American opinion and advancing statehood while young dual citizens remained culturally, socially, and politically tied to Japan and sympathetic to the Axis.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Report on Overseas Japanese Participation and Expatriation in Hawaii
